title: Choose the band page's structure
question: Three structures for the band page, all in the site's existing look. The roll leads with the index card. Keep it, take another, or re-roll.

options.label: Record-store index card
options.lineage: record-store bin dividers and library catalog cards
options.thesis: Each band is a filed card: a purple name tab, typed fields, then the bio on ruled lines.
options.viewport: Name tab and big name; a lavender 'Next show' strip right under it; fields for members, links and photo; bio on ruled lines with its Wikipedia credit.
options.risk: A no-photo, no-bio local band leaves a short card, which reads finished only if the empty fields simply aren't drawn.

options.label: Encyclopedia infobox
options.thesis: A reading column of bio and shows, with a right-hand fact box for photo, origin, members and links.
options.viewport: Name and bio on the left, an upcoming-shows table below; the fact box on the right holds the photo slot, origin, active years, members, past members and links.
options.risk: Familiar to the point of borrowed: it looks like a Wikipedia page, and sparse bands leave an empty-looking box.

options.label: Tour itinerary
options.lineage: the dates on the back of a tour shirt or poster
options.thesis: Shows lead: a huge name, then the Northeast dates as a bold timetable, with who they are underneath.
options.viewport: Name in heavy caps with links on one line; a purple 'Upcoming in the Northeast' bar over date rows (date, town, venue, save); About and Members side by side below.
options.risk: A band with no upcoming shows loses its lead section, so the page must fall back to identity first.
